name: Rebecca Lee Crumpler
record: Crumpler earned her medical degree at the New England Female Medical College. Boston University identifies her as the first Black woman in the United States to earn one.
work: She later cared for people newly freed from slavery in Richmond, Virginia, through the Freedmen’s Bureau.

name: Mary Eliza Mahoney
record: Mahoney graduated from the nursing school at the New England Hospital for Women and Children. The American Nurses Association recognizes her as the first Black graduate nurse in the United States.
work: Thirty years later, she welcomed nurses to the first conference of the National Association of Colored Graduate Nurses.

sources.label: American Nurses Association Hall of Fame

name: Anna Louise James
record: James graduated from the Brooklyn College of Pharmacy in 1908. The following year, she became the first Black woman Connecticut licensed as a pharmacist.
work: She ran a pharmacy in Hartford and later worked at her brother-in-law’s pharmacy in Saybrook.

sources.label: Connecticut Museum of Culture and History

name: Sadie Tanner Mossell Alexander
record: Alexander became the first Black woman to graduate from Penn Law. That same year, Pennsylvania admitted her to its bar, the first Black woman the state authorized to practice law.
work: She practiced estate and family law in Philadelphia. Her father, Aaron Albert Mossell, had graduated from Penn Law in 1888.

name: Clarence “Skip” Ellis
record: Ellis earned his doctorate at the University of Illinois, which identifies him as the first Black American to earn a PhD in computer science.
work: At Illinois he worked on the ILLIAC IV supercomputer, including its software. His record connects to software work through that project.
